newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Refugees pour back into Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Refugees pour back into Rwanda.

text.p: Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees streamed home across the border from Zaire on Saturday for the second straight day, witnesses said.
"The road of death is now a road of hope," said Ray Wilkinson of the U.N. refugee agency, UNHCR.

The UNHCR said the refugees were crossing over into Rwanda at the rate of 12,000 an hour. "Some 100,000 have crossed since yesterday, they are so many we cannot register them," UNHCR spokesman Peter Kessler said.

Witnesses said the road leading west into the heart of Zaire was packed with returning refugees who fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing repisals after a rebel Tutsi movement swept to victory and ended a genocide of up to a million mostly Tutsi people.
"It is an incredible sight, a moving sea of people," Reuter Television cameraman Des Wright said.

Kessler said some 300,000 people had converged on the east Zaire town of Goma and were heading towards the border after the Zairean Banyamulenge rebel movement broke the grip of Hutu gunmen who had prevented them from returning.
